title: Rows loaded equal the source's own total
why: A silent shortfall makes every later number wrong without any error appearing.
action: Stop using the latest figures, re-run the load and compare again.
condition: Reload until the row counts match.

title: Date windows neither overlap nor drop a day
why: The service's end date excludes the day it names, so a plain date range quietly loses a day and overlapping windows count a day twice.
action: Correct the window boundaries and reload.
condition: Correct the window boundaries.

title: Source columns match the data contract
why: A renamed or missing column can pass unnoticed and quietly empty a downstream figure.
action: Update the contract and the engine together, then re-run.
condition: Agree the new columns.

title: The publisher's specification hasn't changed
why: The previous version of this service was retired in late 2025. A changed specification is the earliest warning of the next change.
action: Read what changed and update the data contract if needed.
condition: Read what the publisher changed.

title: Row counts don't fall sharply between runs
why: Results normally only build up, and the window moves by a month at a time. A sudden fall means something has gone wrong upstream, even when each row looks fine.
action: Compare with the source before using the latest figures.
condition: Explain the fall in row counts before using the figures.

title: No source is running on an out-of-date copy
why: The bathing water service doesn't accept requests from the server that runs the nightly check, so a saved copy stands in. A copy is only as good as its date.
action: Take a fresh copy of the season from an ordinary home connection.
condition: Take a fresh copy of the bathing water season before relying on the comparison.

title: Open sampling points have a result in the window
why: The register says a point is open, yet the data is silent. Some are used only on demand, so this is a question for a steward and not a fault.
action: Agree which open points are in use, and record the reason for the rest.
condition: Don't read "open" as "currently sampled".

title: Each stream has its usual volume each month
why: A stream that stops arriving makes a monthly total look like a collapse in sampling.
action: Ask the publisher whether the stream arrives in batches, and leave affected months out of comparisons meanwhile.
condition: Compare months only once each stream has reached its usual volume.

title: Each stream's newest result is within its normal silence
why: One "last updated" date can look fine while whole streams have stopped. Each stream is measured against the longest silence it has shown in the window, with three weeks as the minimum.
action: Flag the stream as late, and find out whether this is normal batch arrival.
condition: State which streams are late in anything built from recent months.

title: Recent months are flagged until they are complete
why: A part-complete month plotted beside full months reads as a collapse.
action: Mark these months as part-complete wherever they are shown.
condition: Mark recent months as part-complete.

title: Each observation address appears once
why: A repeated record is counted twice in every total.
action: Keep one copy, and find out where the second came from.
condition: Remove the duplicates.

title: One value per point, time and thing measured
why: Two different values for the same moment can't both be the answer.
action: Review each pair, and agree which value to use and why.
condition: State how repeated values are handled.

title: Each sampling point has its own label
why: Shared labels make a list of places look shorter than it is, and joining on the label merges different places.
action: Join on the point's code, never its label.
condition: Join on the point's code, never its label.

title: Every result is a number, a limit or a listed word
why: A new word appearing in the result column is the first sign of a change upstream.
action: Add the new word to the list with its meaning, or raise it with the publisher.
condition: Treat unlisted words as unknown.

title: pH is between 0 and 14
why: Outside this range the value isn't a pH at all.
action: Leave the record out, and raise it with the publisher.
condition: Leave these records out.

title: Dates are readable and not in the future
why: A date that can't be read or hasn't happened breaks every time-based figure.
action: Leave the record out, and raise it with the publisher.
condition: Leave these records out.

title: Coordinates are inside the North West
why: Catch-all points carry a stand-in location in the English Channel, so a real sample's true place is unknown.
action: Keep these points off maps and out of place-based averages, and show them separately.
condition: Show stand-in locations separately, never on a map.

title: Codes exist in the official code lists
why: A code nobody can look up has no agreed meaning.
action: Ask the publisher what the code means, and add it to the reference list.
condition: Treat unknown codes as unknown.

title: Result holds a measurement, not a lab status
why: "Sent to sub contract lab" says something happened, not what was found. A real value may follow later.
action: Leave these out of calculations, and watch the ledger for a real value replacing them.
condition: Leave lab status rows out of calculations.

title: Results can go straight into a calculation
why: A plain conversion loses or misreads every "below a limit" result, and that inflates averages. This is a normal way to report results. It needs a stated method, not a correction.
action: Publish the method for below-limit results, and use it everywhere.
condition: Count below-limit results with a stated method. Never drop them.

title: Each code has one unit
why: Mixed units within a code would make any sum meaningless.
action: Hold the affected code back until its unit is confirmed.
condition: Hold the affected code back.

title: Each name means one thing
why: One name can cover two scales. Joining on the name then mixes results that differ by a factor of 100.
action: Join on the code, never the name, and add the distinction to the glossary.
condition: Join on the code, never the name.

title: Results agree with the register
why: The two parts of one service should tell the same story about a point.
action: Raise any disagreement with the publisher.
condition: Use the register's version.

title: Detection limits are stable within what was measured
why: A "below 500" and a "below 0.001" under one name can't share a model column unexplained. Some of this is legitimate, because a strong sample is diluted.
action: Record which limits apply, and keep long-term figures to a stable limit.
condition: Keep trends to one stable limit.

title: pH is usually between 4 and 11
why: Possible, but unusual enough for a person to look at.
action: Review each one. Most will be real.
condition: Review extreme values before relying on them.

title: Water temperature is between -2 and 40 degrees
why: Above this it is more likely an effluent, a typing slip or the wrong unit than a natural water.
action: Review each one against the point's type.
condition: Review extreme values before relying on them.

title: No result is over 1,000 times the usual level
why: One extreme value can dominate an average. Many will be real, and they are worth checking before they drive a headline.
action: Review each one, and consider a median beside the average.
condition: Show a median beside any average.

title: Above-range results are treated as ceilings
why: ">9999999" means at least that much. Strip the sign and a ceiling becomes a measurement that swamps any average.
action: Keep these out of averages, or count them as minimums.
condition: Treat above-range results as minimums.

title: Bathing E. coli matches between the two services
why: Two independent public services agreeing is strong evidence that the data is sound.
action: List the differences for the publisher.
condition: Use one service, and say which.

title: Every bathing point can be linked between services
why: The only link is a five-digit code inside a free-text label. The data agrees, but the key that joins it isn't governed.
action: Keep a governed lookup between the two services.
condition: Keep the comparison to the points that can be linked.

title: Labels hold no apparent personal data
why: Labels run several fields together, including addresses. The source is public, but republishing a home address has to be a deliberate decision.
action: Withhold the label on anything flagged, and link to the source record instead.
condition: Withhold flagged labels.

title: Nothing about to be published holds personal data
why: The last check before anything leaves the building. If this fails, the affected field isn't published.
action: Stop publishing the field and tighten the mask.
condition: Withhold the field.

title: Below-limit share is within what a model can handle
why: When much of a target is only known to be "below something", a model needs special handling, or it learns the limit and not the water.
action: Use a method built for censored targets, or choose a target with less censoring.
condition: Use a method built for censored targets.

title: Samples cover the whole week
why: A model can't learn about hours it has never seen. Sampling happens in working hours, so nights and weekends are almost absent.
action: State plainly that predictions apply to weekday working hours only.
condition: Limit predictions to the hours the data covers.

title: Enough repeat samples per point
why: Under one sample a month, a model can't separate a place's pattern from noise.
action: Train only on points with regular history, and say how few that leaves.
condition: Train only on points with regular history.

title: Clock times are real times, not defaults
why: When one minute takes a large share of a stream's samples, it looks like a convention and not a time. Time-of-day can't then be used as an input. Why this happens is unconfirmed.
action: Ask the publisher what these stamps mean, and leave time-of-day out for the streams affected.
condition: Leave time of day out for affected streams.

title: The change ledger has run long enough to trust
why: The publisher says records may change as quality assurance continues, and refreshes monthly. Until the ledger has covered a full cycle, nobody can say how often published figures move.
action: Keep running. This clears itself after 35 days.
condition: Wait for the ledger to cover one full monthly refresh.

title: Licence statements agree
why: The service, its catalogue record and its sister service should give the same licence. A figure can't be signed off on an unclear right to reuse it.
action: Record which statement is relied on, and ask the publisher to align them.
condition: Record which licence statement you rely on.

title: There are no gaps in the run history
why: A control that didn't run looks exactly like a control that found nothing, unless the gaps are counted.
action: Find out why the run was missed. Scheduled jobs can be disabled without warning.
condition: State any gaps in the run history.

title: Every rule caught its planted defect at the last check
why: A check that can't fail proves nothing. Each night a defect is planted in a private copy to prove each rule still fires.
action: Treat the rule that missed its defect as broken until it is fixed.
condition: Fix the rule that missed its defect.
